content: "May I pose the question of the difference between government and culture. Many things like how to take care of the land, schooling, languages, and other things have very significant cultural contexts how much government intervention is to much when it comes to those things."
`There's so many elves, might be difficult to pick you out at a glance. But looking for a purple frog, or a white bird, or a black cat, pretty easy to do.`
Irynx lands on Sabrine's shoulder. "He's already walked off, Sabby. I think it's been said."

(that's Kukudh following him, so)
Sabrine shrugs. 'Anyway. We need to absolutely respect other people, we need to absolutely respect nature. If we don't respect either of these our descendants will have a bad time.'
'Our goal should be to make things better for those who come after us.'

"Anything divided is vulnerable to conflicts and instability, be them branches or states. I suggest we unify our government and lands instead. Checks and balances can still be observed between the government and the governed and our lands can still be held by a strong authority."

"Sowing seeds in a garden we'll never get to see grow. I agree Sabrine. I think there's a way we could look at adding the right of nature to our descendants. Meaning that we will leave nature in a way that is sustainable for our descendants to see. An addition to the bill of rights"
"A division of labor is simply how the world works. God's, people, offices. They must be divided to conquer the most amount of challenges. The goal is what we unify for and with"
"What is, isn't always what ought to be."
"We have the power to change how the world works. There is strength in unity, so we should be united at all fronts."

"I do want to fly this back to the Triumvirate discussion. As messy is my history with hags, the rule of three serves the old bags well. Not pointing to an answer here, just adding to the idea. I mean, we're not exactly hags."

"A centralized system with the ability for tiers of government with individual needs met within states. I agree we shouldn't have something like a loose federation. Which is why there are several articles notated on the functions in tandem and what authority supersedes which in the proposal."

"I may not be able to word it in an official way, and I speak both as a follower of Mender's path and a swarmkeeper for whom that path is natural, but my overall point about nature is: we're inevitable to expand, that's how all people do. We will take resources from nature to keep living. But, as Sabrine said, we can and should do it such that the balance is not harmed. We have great thinkers and doers among us, we're capable of it. We shouldn't need the treaty with the Wardens for this - that's why I believe treating the wild world beyond our borders with respect is something we should accept. I believe that is all of my point in this topic."
"Three branches of government, three heads of state"
"I'll make an amendment to the proposal. I think what you have to say is important that we don't allow this to slip past our sights"

"The rule of three works with the hags, but I loathe to compare our new country to them. We are not creatures of malice kept in check by others as evil as us. One leader is a much better rallying point than 3. Multiple voices of authority just serve to confuse."
'But then if that leader is corrupted, what happens then?'
"On the chopping block?"
"If you wish for checks and balances, the balance between governed and governor is simple and elegant. We don't need any more complicated system."
"The people rally together against them, or they vote them out if we are to follow that system."
"Like in my airship metaphor, Cap. I do my part with the engine, and I'll leave the rest of the job to the rest of the crew better suited for it."

Fiona speaks up. "I agree with the concept of checks and balances, but I worry about public servants being tasked with doing that as well as their other jobs. I worry about them either focusing too much on watching other officials or not enough. I agree with my husband that there should be officials seperate from any senator or representative who's sole job is to ensure power is now abused."
"And our way of choosing our leader should be made so that corruption doesn't take a foothold on our sears of power."

"Why make a new body of government tasked with watching over the government. That will be a vector of corruption. The people under the government can already take the responsibility of keeping the government in place. You praise the power of the people, then let us employ it."
"We should let the people vote for their leader. We are all tired to of so-called leaders who don't have the support of the people."
"You suggest using the people's power here, then why not use them for checks and balances as well. I still see no need for the three branches."

Finn nods in acknowledgement of Roy before looking to the Kelly's

"An additional system? Would this system be an additional elected group or appointed by someone? Where would they be able to fit into a position like this where they too are kept in check"
"Arcania is one big airship," Irynx perches on Roy's head. "We choose our captain, who we know is best for the job, understands the strengths of their crew, their cabinet."
"Captain Finn speaks wisely, we shouldn't be adding more systems that will serve only to complicate things further."
"And a system of a sole central authority kept in check by the governed has strength in its simplicity.

"Speaker, everything is corruptible. But good and bad isn't a binary and we shouldn't treat it as such. Mistake will happen and the people will be able to act as a check and balance system through their votes. If they don't like a leader, that person won't get reelected."

"To address their needs. The legislative branch holds the most power and most dilution as they represent the most pure form of a democratic enterprise. The judicial follows suit similarly, but has the power to interpret and discuss enforcement options of it. The executive being the ones that put in the power to enforce it. Without the bodies of congress, we wouldn't have the representation of the people in its purest organized form. That is why they are designed to be codependent and harmonious"

"They would be kept in check directly and elected by the people. It would be easier to focus just on their one job as interested citizens than having to focus both on the content of representative's jobs and they're accountability at once."
The speaker nods at the fey. "That is exactly what I was thinking of. Our leaders should focus on leading and not be burdened by regulating their peers in office."

"The check on their power allows the congress to keep the enforcing powers from abusing them. Judicial is limited by their ability to make law or change it. While the House must function with the needs and wants of a great many people they represent. Their beaucracy is their check and balance that can be checked additionally so by executive or stopped in judicial from moving forward"
Kegbot/Eliza feels lost in all the conversations and just keeps her copy in hand, reading it over again.
"Bureaucracy adds unnecessary complexities that will serve only to delay our government in times of need."
"They're a small bird." Replies Ryan. "Either they're moving about a lot or are obscured by other bodies." He waves his hand, shooing Kukudh like one might an ordinary pigeon or mosquito.

"The legislative body would have the job of making law. The executive for leading, addressing the public, creating progressive opportunities, and the judicial is integral for keeping the processes ratified, cohesive and just"

"Its because they have to work together to share the power that they are forced to check each others power. Running a nation requires a great deal of complexity and many people will be needed to make it run smoothly."
"I disagree with your fundamentals. It is the exact thing we need to set us apart from that of a monarchy or dictatorship"
Vivica nods agreeing with Finn

"The world is not so cutthroat that we all must be at each other's. These bodies share the same goals and ideals of the people they represent. It's is a matter of how they enact the change is their biggest charge rather than looking out for who tries to take power"

"A dictatorship run by someone competent is a whole lot better than a republic of fools. We should focus on finding a way to put the competent in charge instead of planning for failsafes in case the foolish get to lead.",
"Our priority needs to be to the people and this is how we make sure we don't leave them with another King George."
"I'm sorry speaker but what you suggest is a slippery slope that has not been found to end well"
"It would not function well when the foundation of our independence is on that of free will and equal representation"
"You complain about corruption, yet argue for a dictatorship!? Absolutely ridiculous."
"And what you suggest is a whole new slipper slope entirely, one that ends with an ineffective government unable to implement new laws because it is busy fighting itself."

"There is no corrupt system, the people who are running it is what allows for corruption. Do not villify the system because of the acts of someone incompetent. One central authority is less vectors for corruption, let us focus in strengthening that."

"Please" he holds out the paper. "Point exactly where the slippery slope is. What you will instead find is a well manifested and detailed process of a system meant to persist and not worry about whether or not the morals or secret agendas of someone is there."
"Where in this will they fight."

"The slipper slope starts the moment you proposed divisions. Divisions put people against each other. And if not intentionally, the time needed to verify every single step will render the system unable to work. There are unnecessary complexities that can be handled by a central authority."

"So you didn't read it? The proposal of a system is not indicative of its actual process. You are arguing another issue altogether without solutions to the working basis of a solution in front of you"
"You're assuming that these divisions are going against each other, they actually to help fill the holes and skills the others are lacking."

"As I said, everything is corruptible but a corrupt dictatorship is a whole lot harder to fix than a corrupted republic. However we are fighting for a mixed system of a democratic republic. I have yet to see an actual proposal from you, Speeker, and I find it harder and harder to debate with you when you're solutions suggest to ignore the will of the people."
"A Midaskian system" Finn pipes up

"If you wish to argue the specifics, I bring up my point against your justice system. You write in the use of magics like the zone of truth but yet write a jury. Charm spells and other such magic would suffice for finding the truth. The midaskian system is written as if we are in a world where magic and gods do not exist, but that is not the case. We have ways to ensure strength that does not rely on mere mortal effort.
"Truth is not judgment. You can lay out the facts and hundreds of people will see it hundreds of ways. I believe that's the purpose of the jury. To determine judgment with the truth."

"A situation where a central authority needs to be stopped just involves removing one person. How is that harder than fixing a system where multiple people are corrupt. A central authority doesn't mandate disenfranchising the masses."
"Yes Irynx you are absolutely correct."
"And proper judgement comes from knowing the truth. As long as the truth is out, judgement will come. We don't need a system of special judges."
"A coup d'etat is not a reasonable solution  everytime we get a bad leader."
"The system is built to be blind, to be truthful and transparent and to be incorruptible unlike the people that will inevitably inhabit it."
"If staging a coup is the only way you can think of to remove an innefective leader, then the Mender's call for more creativity from this body rings true."

"one leader would also most likely become corrupt from the temptation of power. This system with everyone given equal rights and rules allows that temptation to stay tame and look toward everyone's goal. Like a party where everyone has their roles in going into a dungeon! We all make sure we don't get hurt! If one tries to hurt someone else in the party, the rest are there to stop it."
"I think the mender's *lessons* from experience show us exactly why we cannot follow his examples or ideas"
Eliza kinda looks down feeling a little dumb using simple analogies to describe large topics
"We have easier ways of finding the truth, yes, but determining what we can do with it is different, more difficult. Especially when the truth is complicated."
Finn smiles at the analogy from Eliza
"Then keeping the courts open to the people should suffice, but that does not stand against a central authority."
Liberty Hall in the Stands
The stands and seating of Liberty Hall designed for discussion on the finer and quieter points and interpretations of ideas
Finn writes down Roy and Sabrine's ideas onto his draft and works on wordsmithing

Vivica passes out a document to those in the stands. 
``` A QUICK GUIDE TO RESTORATIVE JUSTICE: 
Definition: a system of criminal justice which focuses on the rehabilitation of offenders through reconciliation with victims and the community at large. 

• Seeks to repair the harm done
• Emphasizes accountability, making amends, and if agreed upon, facilitated meeting between offenders and victims.
• Seeks to empower victims and meet their needs
• The goal is to heal, and prevent repeat offenders from being cycled through the system
• Often applies indigenous practices of council and justice when dealing out consequences
• If needed, a prison would be used for reintegration into society by giving them tools to succeed
• Community restoration and involvement is key to success 

Examples:
• Community service 
• Restitution 
• Victim-offender reconciliation ```
<@260820438026813440> (since you asked for it.)
"Kinda rude, but not wrong."
"this is a great idea Vivica! Although, what do we do about hostile criminals that could possibly harm the victims? Or do I have the wrong understanding of this?
"Its covered in section V of our drafted constitution. Punitive measures can be taken in extreme cases."
"Look, we didn't fight this war and watch an entire people get slaughtered for us to run right back into a monarchy with an immortal king"
"I would say hostile criminals that refuse the restorative system would fall under an extreme circumstance."
"that's what I thought, but isn't the goal to make them both repay and learn to improve themselves? Would there be a special case for trying to rehabilitate them?"
"That's something that is inherently hostile and dangerous to the nation we have built thus far and the values we have fought for"
"I know that if things get too hasty, that section V protects, but just wondering how we could handle someone like that for this type of system"
"What I like about restorative measures is that they are often case by case. Addressing the issues, how the incident came to happen and a council of people working towards a solution."
"Freedom is red, we paid its price. Unity... unity is different. It should be kind, fair, all good things."
"Built and governed by the people it represents in their shared values" he nods

"You say power corrupts, so why then are systems excempt from the corrosiveness of power. You argue for staving off an entire group of people from the grasps of corruption, and I argue for focusing on one. Surely it is easier to keep a signle ruler in check than multiple branches of government."

"However it only works if the offender chooses to go through the system and face their natural consequences. There will likely always be a case or two where someone refuses to work with the system that seeks to help them as well."
